audiences.executive: Databases delivered in minutes to the teams that need them, protected and patched to one standard.
audiences.technical: Provisioning, cloning, patching and point-in-time recovery for each engine, as self-service within guardrails.
audiences.financial: Fewer full copies of production data, licences counted where databases actually run, less DBA time on routine work.

people: Security, for masked copies of production data

objections.says: Our DBAs will not give up control.
objections.clarify: Which tasks do they want to keep, and which take their time today?
objections.answer: They set the standards and approve; routine provisioning, patching and cloning become self-service within those standards.
objections.prove: A developer gets a masked copy of a production database in minutes, under a policy the DBAs set.

objections.says: Our databases are too critical to move.
objections.clarify: Which ones, on which engines and versions, and with which recovery objective?
objections.answer: Start with test and development copies, then the less critical, with recovery tested at each step.
objections.prove: Restore a database to a point in time chosen by the DBA, and check it.

objections.clarify: How are database licences counted today, and on how many cores?
objections.answer: Count licences against where databases will run; consolidating can reduce the cores to license.
objections.prove: Compare the cores the databases need on the new platform with the cores licensed today.
